# doing minor or test analyses

```{r}
## are lever presses at day 1 at floor?

inc_sessions %>%
  filter(session == 1) -> inc_sess1

shapiro.test(inc_sess1$lever)
t.test(inc_sess1$lever, mu = 0)
wilcox.test(inc_sess1$lever, mu = 0)
```

```{r}
## how does sex play a role in the models?
# aka compare to hannah's results

# collapse across within-session time
inc_sessions <- inc_dbl_scr %>%
  group_by(subject, session, drug, sex) %>%
  summarise(
    beam = mean(beam),
    sniff = mean(sniff),
    groom = mean(groom),
    shake = mean(shake),
    lever = mean(lever)
  )

lev_test <- lmer(lever ~ session * drug * sex + (1|subject),data = inc_sessions)
summary(lev_test)

lev_test <- lmer(groom ~ session * drug * sex + (1|subject),data = inc_sessions)
summary(lev_test)

lev_test <- lmer(beam ~ session * drug * sex + (1|subject),data = inc_sessions)
summary(lev_test)

lev_test <- lmer(sniff ~ session * drug * sex + (1|subject),data = inc_sessions)
summary(lev_test)

# no three way interactions with sex
```


```{r}
# sniffing vs seeking combinations

# calculate a sneek variable which is sniff + seek
# for heroin rodents whose seek = NaN, convert to zero
inc_dbl_scr %>%
  mutate(seek = ifelse(is.nan(seek), 0 , seek),
         sneek = seek + sniff) -> inc_sneek

# re-run all behaviors by lever
lev_sneek <- lmer(lever ~ groom + sneek + shake + beam + (1|subject),data = inc_sneek)
summary(lev_sneek) # results hold

# seperate out by drug to avoid triple interactions
inc_sneek %>%
  filter(drug == 1) -> inc_sneek_heroin

inc_sneek %>%
  filter(drug == 2) -> inc_sneek_sucrose

# re-run drug specific models
lev_sneek_heroin <- lmer(lever ~ beam + groom + shake + sneek + (1|subject),data = inc_sneek_heroin)
summary(lev_sneek_heroin) # results hold as this variable didn't change

lev_sneek_sucrose <- lmer(lever ~ beam + groom + shake + sneek + (1|subject),data = inc_sneek_sucrose)
summary(lev_sneek_sucrose) # results hold, sneek goes down (beta = -0.3) / sniff beta = -0.29
```


```{r}
rand_slp_test <- lmer(lever ~ sniff + (1 + sniff|subject),data = inc_dbl_scr)
summary(rand_slp_test)

# Extract random effects
random_effects <- ranef(rand_slp_test)$subject

# Convert random effects to a dataframe
random_effects_df <- as.data.frame(random_effects)

# Add subject IDs
random_effects_df$subject <- rownames(random_effects)

# Plot random slopes for IV1
ggplot(random_effects_df, aes(x = subject, y = sniff)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") + 
  labs(title = "Random Slopes for Sniffing by Subject", 
       x = "Subject", 
       y = "Random Slope for Sniffing") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
summary(lmer(lever ~ sniff*session + (1|subject), data = inc_dbl_scr))
```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)

lev_test <- lmer(shake ~ session + drug + time + session:drug + drug:time + (1|subject),data = inc_dbl_scr)
summary(lev_test)

emms <- emmeans(lev_test, ~ session * drug)
emms_df <- as.data.frame(emms)



# Modify the levels of drug to label them as "Heroin" and "Sucrose"
emms_df$drug <- factor(emms_df$drug, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Heroin", "Sucrose"))

# Create the plot with customizations
ggplot(emms_df, aes(x = session, y = emmean, color = drug, group = drug)) +
  geom_line(size = 3) +  # Change line thickness here
  geom_point(size = 6) +   # Change point size here
  labs(x = "Session", y = "shakes", 
       color = "Drug", 
       title = "Interaction of Session and Drug on Shakes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Heroin" = rgb(1, 0.4, 0, 0.5), "Sucrose" = rgb(0, 0.8, 1, 0.5))) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 15), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),   # Adjust x-axis label text size here
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15)) # Adjust y-axis label text size here
  # scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:5, limits = c(1, 5))

# Resize the plot
# ggsave("session_drug_interaction_plot.png", width = 8, height = 6)  # Save with specific dimensions
```
